subject: Azure private plan — license matrix & procurement path
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@cardinalhealth.com>, Jared Thompson <jared.thompson@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Marketplace Ops <marketplace-ops@microsoft.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Azure private plan — license matrix & procurement path

Hi Jared / procurement team —

Thanks for the time on Friday. As discussed, I’m attaching our proposed license matrix for the Azure private offer so your procurement and legal teams can map entitlements to your internal SKUs and billing flows. Key items we want to align on:

- Entitlement tiers (Seat vs. Concurrent vs. Token-based) and whether Cardinal prefers a fixed-capacity SKU or metered usage.
- Bill-to / remit-to details for the marketplace private plan.
- Any required PO fields and invoicing cadence (monthly vs. quarterly).
- If Cardinal requires publisher seller authorization or marketplace publisher tokens from Microsoft to complete the private offer.

Attachment: license_matrix_cardinal_v1.xlsx (summary tab + detailed mapping)

Next steps: If you can send back a redline with procurement/PO expectations, we’ll prepare the DocuSign and ask Microsoft to provision the private listing with the SKU mapping.

Cheers,

Mina Haddad
Senior Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Susan Liu <susan.liu@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jared Thompson <jared.thompson@cardinalhealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Azure private plan — license matrix & procurement path

Hi Mina —

Thanks for the matrix. We reviewed it with Legal and Procurement and added a redline with two primary asks: 1) clarify how overages are charged when using token-based billing, and 2) confirm that the private plan will respect our existing PO number fields for invoice reconciliation.

We also flagged the commercial exhibit to request a 60-day invoice payment term (Cardinal prefers net-60). Please see our annotated doc attached: procurement_request_cardinal_redline.docx.

One point of clarification: will Redwood accept purchase orders that reference the Marketplace private SKU (we generate the PO but need the SKU tied back to the invoice)? If so, please explain how the marketplace billing flow maps back to Redwood’s remit-to.

We’d like to have a mutually executable version by next week to align with our quarter close.

Regards,

Susan Liu
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Cardinal Health
susan.liu@cardinalhealth.com

Attachment: procurement_request_cardinal_redline.docx

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 10:07:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Azure private plan — license matrix & procurement path

Mina —

Quick internal notes after reviewing Cardinal’s redline:

- Overages: we recommend offering a capped overage rate tied to token blocks (e.g., $X per 10k tokens) and a notification cadence. That should satisfy Procurement while keeping unit economics predictable.
- Payment terms: net-60 will push our cash conversion but we can agree for enterprise deals with a 1.5% fee to offset the longer term, or request an initial prepayment for the first 30 days. Want guidance from Finance (Karthik) and Revenue Ops (Rishi).
- Marketplace flow: Microsoft requires the private offer to reference the listing SKU. Microsoft will invoice Cardinal and remit to Redwood per the marketplace agreement; however, we must confirm the remit-to mapping in the marketplace onboarding form (publisher token required).

Action items:
1) Mina: propose capped overage language and specific dollar blocks to present back to Susan.
2) Karthik: confirm whether Redwood can accept net-60 with a small financing fee or whether we need a prepay.
3) Rishi: prepare a brief ledger example showing how marketplace invoicing ties to our revenue recognition and remittance.

I’ll join any call with Cardinal if helpful.

-Jonas
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Susan Liu <susan.liu@cardinalhealth.com>, Jared Thompson <jared.thompson@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Marketplace Ops <marketplace-ops@microsoft.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2027 08:56:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private plan — license matrix & procurement path

Hi Susan / Jared —

Thanks for the redline and the clear asks. We can accommodate Cardinal’s requirements with the following proposal: 

- Overages: capped at $250 per 10k tokens above committed usage; notification at 70% and 90% of committed capacity. We can add an option to convert to an auto-increment block if you prefer predictability.
- Payment terms: we can accept net-60 for this transaction but will add a 1.25% financing fee to offset extended receivables. Alternatively, a 30-day prepayment option removes the fee.
- Marketplace SKU / PO mapping: attached sku_mapping_azure.csv maps each entitlement row to a Marketplace private SKU. Microsoft will need the listing ID and publisher token to ensure the PO references the SKU on the invoice.

DocuSign link (proposal + commercial exhibit): https://www.docusign.com/en/link/abc123-docsign-cardinal

Please confirm if the overage cap and financing fee are acceptable. Once we have your okay, I’ll work with Microsoft (cc’d) to provision the private listing and request the publisher token for final DocuSign execution.

Attachment: sku_mapping_azure.csv

Best,

Mina Haddad
Senior Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marketplace Ops <marketplace-ops@microsoft.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Susan Liu <susan.liu@cardinalhealth.com>, Jared Thompson <jared.thompson@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Sep 2027 11:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private plan — license matrix & procurement path

Hi Mina / Susan —

We reviewed the sku_mapping_azure.csv and can provision a private offer for Cardinal Health. Two items we need from Redwood to complete provisioning: 1) Azure Marketplace listing ID (if you already have a private listing, provide the listing GUID), and 2) Publisher token / seller authorization form (we’ll send the publisher form to your technical contact).

Once those are provided we can:
- Create the private offer referencing the SKUs you provided.
- Associate the private offer to Cardinal’s tenant so their PO will reference the SKU on the invoice.
- Confirm the remit-to information in the marketplace onboarding so Microsoft remits per the agreed flow.

We’ll also flag the net-60 + financing fee in our internal approval path; Microsoft accepts these on a per-deal basis and may require additional vendor profiling.

Next steps (concise):
1) Mina: send listing GUID + completed publisher token form to marketplace-ops@microsoft.com.
2) Susan / Jared: confirm acceptance of overage cap + 1.25% fee (or indicate prepay option).
3) Redwood: once private offer is created, we’ll share the draft invoice flow and test a dummy PO to validate reconciliation fields.

Thanks,
Marketplace Ops Team
Microsoft Corporation
marketplace-ops@microsoft.com
